annotations.annotation_text: Swiftian presence "swift" on page 198 ("Anna Livia Plurabelle"): the Dean of St. Patrick's Cathedral haunts this passage within the two washerwomen gossiping on opposite banks of the darkening Liffey, 500+ river names woven into the text, metamorphosis into elm and stone. His dual lovers Stella and Vanessa mirror Issy's split personalities, while his savage satire infuses the Age of Gods (closing) dream with political and scatological ferocity.
sources: Ehrenpreis, Irvin. Swift: The Man, His Works, and the Age. https://archive.org/details/swiftmanhisworks01ehre

annotations.annotation_text: HCE manifestation "H.C.E" on page 198 within "Anna Livia Plurabelle": here the universal father-figure Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker appears in the context of the two washerwomen gossiping on opposite banks of the darkening Liffey, 500+ river names woven into the text, metamorphosis into elm and stone. During this Age of Gods (closing) phase, HCE embodies the patriarch whose guilt, grandeur, and fall drive the cyclical dream forward.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
McHugh, Roland. The Sigla of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/siglaoffinnegans0000mchu
